section_title: What is authority in Christ meant to accomplish?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 7 You are looking at outward appearances. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should remind himself that we belong to Christ just as much as he does. 8 For even if I boast somewhat excessively about the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.

9 I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters. 10 For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.” 11 Such people should consider that what we are in our letters when absent, we will be in our actions when present.

context_lines: Paul asks the Corinthians to look beyond outward appearances. Anyone confident of belonging to Christ should recognize that Paul and his fellow workers belong to Him too. The critics’ confidence in themselves gives them no basis for dismissing his relationship to Christ.

Paul then names the purpose of the authority the Lord gave him: building the Corinthians up. His confidence in that calling explains his firm words. The community’s good is the purpose he sets before them.
He quotes the criticism being made of him. Some find his letters forceful while describing his personal presence and speaking dismissively. These are their judgments, reported as part of the dispute.

Paul answers that his conduct in person will match his words from a distance. He wants them to take the letters seriously and respond, knowing that his authority will also be exercised when he arrives.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly read this as a defense of Paul’s authority and its purpose of strengthening the church. [Wesley’s notes on verses 7–10](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-second-epistle-to-the-corinthians/) address judgments based on appearances; the [USCCB notes on verses 7–10](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/2corinthians/10) likewise emphasize the intended good of Paul’s ministry for the community.
god_plan_lines: [Ephesians 4:11–16](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/4.htm) describes Christ giving workers to equip His people and build up His body. The goal is maturity in Him, with the whole body growing in love as each part does its work.

That wider purpose helps explain the authority Paul describes here. Christ is forming a people who know Him, stand firm in the truth and serve one another. Leadership belongs within that work of growth.
